items.publisher: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
items.title: Myths and Facts about COVID-19 Vaccines
items.snippet_en: The CDC confirms that COVID-19 vaccines do not contain microchips and are not used to track people's movement. Vaccines work only to stimulate the immune system to produce antibodies and contain no tracking components.

items.publisher: Kementerian Komunikasi dan Informatika RI (Kominfo) via Pemprov DKI Jakarta (Jalahoaks)
items.title: [HOAKS] - Vaksin COVID-19 Memiliki Chip Yang Dapat Melacak Keberadaan Orang
items.snippet_en: Official spokespersons stated that claims regarding COVID-19 vaccines containing tracking microchips are false. Tracking elements and barcodes exist strictly on packaging and distribution logistics to track vaccine vials, not inside the vaccines administered to recipients.

items.title: Covid-19 vaccines do not contain tracking devices
items.snippet_en: Infectious disease specialists and health regulators in the United States and Canada confirmed that authorized COVID-19 vaccines do not contain microchips or tracking devices, debunking claims circulating on social media.

items.title: COVID-19 Vaccines Don’t Have Microchips
items.snippet_en: The fact-check confirms COVID-19 vaccines do not contain microchips. Claims stemmed from misleading interpretations of optional RFID tags used on external syringe packaging for supply chain tracking, which carry no patient data and cannot be injected.

items.title: COVID-19 vaccine myths debunked
items.snippet_en: Mayo Clinic medical directors confirmed that there are no microchips in COVID-19 vaccines, nor any mechanism to track or gather personal information through vaccination.

outputs.notes_en: All sources directly contradict the claim that COVID-19 vaccines contain microchips to track individuals.
